+/// How a [`SelectChoice`] renders inside an inquire menu: `label — detail`.
+#[derive(Clone)]
+struct ChoiceItem {
+    index: usize,
+    text: String,
+}
+
+impl fmt::Display for ChoiceItem {
+    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
+        f.write_str(&self.text)
+    }
+}
+
+fn choice_item(index: usize, choice: &SelectChoice) -> ChoiceItem {
+    let text = match choice.detail.as_deref().filter(|d| !d.trim().is_empty()) {
+        Some(detail) => format!("{} — {detail}", choice.label),
+        None => choice.label.clone(),
+    };
+    ChoiceItem { index, text }
+}
+
+/// The shared inquire theme, derived from the [`Tone`] palette: cyan prompt
+/// marker and selection, dim help text. Colorless when the stdout color gate
+/// (`--plain`, `NO_COLOR`, dumb terminal) is off.
+fn render_config() -> RenderConfig<'static> {
+    if !ui::enabled(Stream::Stdout) {
+        return RenderConfig::empty();
+    }
+    RenderConfig::default_colored()
+        .with_prompt_prefix(Styled::new("?").with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
+        .with_answered_prompt_prefix(Styled::new("✓").with_fg(Color::LightGreen))
+        .with_highlighted_option_prefix(Styled::new("›").with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
+        .with_selected_option(Some(
+            StyleSheet::new()
+                .with_fg(Color::LightCyan)
+                .with_attr(Attributes::BOLD),
+        ))
+        .with_help_message(StyleSheet::new().with_fg(Color::DarkGrey))
+        .with_answer(StyleSheet::new().with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
+}

+fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
+    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
+    let mut chars = text.chars();
+    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
+        if c == '\u{1b}' {
+            if chars.next() == Some('[') {
+                for next in chars.by_ref() {
+                    if ('@'..='~').contains(&next) {
+                        break;
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            continue;
+        }
+        out.push(c);
+    }
+    out

1	//! One prompt engine for every interactive surface.
2	//!
3	//! On a TTY (and unless `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE` is set) prompts render
4	//! through `inquire` — arrow-key selects with hints, styled confirms, and
5	//! text inputs themed to the shared [`Tone`] palette. Off-TTY, in line mode,
6	//! and under `--plain`-style gating, everything falls back to the original
7	//! numbered line prompts so scripts and tests keep byte-stable behavior.
8	//! Esc cancels: a menu with a choice whose id is `"cancel"` resolves to that
9	//! choice; otherwise the prompt errors with `Interrupted`, which callers
10	//! surface as a blocked verdict.
11

32	            detail: None,
33	        }
34	    }

57	/// How a [`SelectChoice`] renders inside an inquire menu: `label — detail`.

64	impl fmt::Display for ChoiceItem {
65	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
66	        f.write_str(&self.text)
67	    }
68	}

70	fn choice_item(index: usize, choice: &SelectChoice) -> ChoiceItem {
71	    let text = match choice.detail.as_deref().filter(|d| !d.trim().is_empty()) {
72	        Some(detail) => format!("{} — {detail}", choice.label),
73	        None => choice.label.clone(),
74	    };
75	    ChoiceItem { index, text }
76	}

78	/// The shared inquire theme, derived from the [`Tone`] palette: cyan prompt
79	/// marker and selection, dim help text. Colorless when the stdout color gate
80	/// (`--plain`, `NO_COLOR`, dumb terminal) is off.
81	fn render_config() -> RenderConfig<'static> {
82	    if !ui::enabled(Stream::Stdout) {
83	        return RenderConfig::empty();
84	    }
85	    RenderConfig::default_colored()
86	        .with_prompt_prefix(Styled::new("?").with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
87	        .with_answered_prompt_prefix(Styled::new("✓").with_fg(Color::LightGreen))
88	        .with_highlighted_option_prefix(Styled::new("›").with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
89	        .with_selected_option(Some(
90	            StyleSheet::new()
91	                .with_fg(Color::LightCyan)
92	                .with_attr(Attributes::BOLD),
93	        ))
94	        .with_help_message(StyleSheet::new().with_fg(Color::DarkGrey))
95	        .with_answer(StyleSheet::new().with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
96	}

98	fn interactive() -> bool {
99	    io::stdin().is_terminal()
100	        && io::stdout().is_terminal()
101	        && std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE").is_none()
102	}

105	    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted, "prompt cancelled").into()
106	}

108	pub(crate) fn open(message: &str, _default: Option<&str>) -> Result<String> {
109	    if interactive() {
110	        let trimmed = message.trim_end().trim_end_matches(':').trim_end();
111	        return match inquire::Text::new(trimmed)
112	            .with_render_config(render_config())
113	            .prompt()
114	        {
115	            Ok(value) => Ok(value.trim().to_string()),
116	            Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled | InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => {
117	                Err(cancelled())
118	            }
119	            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
120	        };
121	    }
122	    print!("{}", ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Prompt, "?"));
123	    print!(" {message}");
124	    io::stdout().flush()?;
125	    let mut input = String::new();
126	    io::stdin().read_line(&mut input)?;
127	    Ok(input.trim_end_matches(&['\r', '\n'][..]).to_string())
128	}

130	pub(crate) fn select_one(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Result<SelectChoice> {
131	    if prompt.choices.is_empty() {
132	        return Err(
133	            io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "select prompt has no choices").into(),
134	        );
135	    }
136	    if interactive() {
137	        return select_one_interactive(prompt);
138	    }
139	    select_one_line(prompt)
140	}

143	    let items = prompt

235	pub(crate) fn confirm(question: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Result<bool> {
236	    if interactive() {

240	            .prompt()
241	        {

244	                Err(cancelled())
245	            }
246	            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),

250	    loop {
251	        let answer = open_line(&format!("{question} {marker}: "))?;
252	        if let Some(value) = parse_confirm_answer(&answer, default_yes) {
253	            return Ok(value);
254	        }
255	        println!("Please answer y or n.");
256	    }

259	fn parse_select_answer(answer: &str, default: usize, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {
260	    if len == 0 {
261	        return None;
262	    }
263	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
264	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
265	        return Some(default.saturating_sub(1).min(len - 1));
266	    }
267	    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
268	    if (1..=len).contains(&value) {
269	        Some(value - 1)
270	    } else {
271	        None
272	    }
273	}
274	
275	fn parse_confirm_answer(answer: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Option<bool> {
276	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
277	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
278	        return Some(default_yes);
279	    }
280	    match trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
281	        "y" | "yes" => Some(true),
282	        "n" | "no" => Some(false),
283	        _ => None,
284	    }
285	}

287	/// Prompt for a number in `range`, re-prompting (never erroring) on empty input
288	/// (which takes `default`), non-numeric input, or an out-of-range value. Use this
289	/// for count-style prompts instead of `open(...).parse()?`, which aborts the whole
290	/// command on a typo.
291	pub(crate) fn ask_number(
292	    label: &str,
293	    range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
294	    default: usize,
295	) -> Result<usize> {
296	    if interactive() {
297	        let start = *range.start();
298	        let end = *range.end();
299	        return match inquire::CustomType::<usize>::new(label)
300	            .with_render_config(render_config())
301	            .with_default(default)
302	            .with_help_message(&format!("{start} to {end}"))
303	            .with_validator(move |value: &usize| {
304	                if (start..=end).contains(value) {
305	                    Ok(inquire::validator::Validation::Valid)
306	                } else {
307	                    Ok(inquire::validator::Validation::Invalid(
308	                        format!("enter a number from {start} to {end}").into(),
309	                    ))
310	                }
311	            })
312	            .prompt()
313	        {
314	            Ok(value) => Ok(value),
315	            Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled | InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => {
316	                Err(cancelled())
317	            }
318	            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
319	        };
320	    }
321	    loop {
322	        let answer = open_line(&format!("{label} [{default}]: "))?;
323	        if let Some(value) = parse_number_in_range(&answer, &range, default) {
324	            return Ok(value);
325	        }
326	        println!(
327	            "Please enter a number from {} to {}.",
328	            range.start(),
329	            range.end()
330	        );
331	    }
332	}
333	
334	fn parse_number_in_range(
335	    answer: &str,
336	    range: &std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
337	    default: usize,
338	) -> Option<usize> {
339	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
340	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
341	        return Some(default);
342	    }
343	    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
344	    if range.contains(&value) {
345	        Some(value)
346	    } else {
347	        None
348	    }
349	}

1	//! Login-state probing for subscription CLI providers.
2	//!
3	//! Binary presence says "installed", not "usable": a user with `claude` on
4	//! PATH but no login sails through setup and hits raw subprocess stderr
5	//! mid-run. Descriptors may declare an `[auth_probe]` (a local status
6	//! subcommand such as `claude auth status`); this module runs it with a
7	//! timeout and classifies the result.
8	//!
9	//! Classification is deliberately fail-open: only an explicit logged-out
10	//! marker (or a logged-in marker that is absent while a logged-out marker
11	//! matches) yields `NotLoggedIn`. Anything ambiguous — unsupported
12	//! subcommand on an older CLI, unexpected output shape, timeout — is
13	//! `Unknown`, and callers treat `Unknown` exactly as they treated binary
14	//! presence before this probe existed.
15	
16	use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
17	use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
18	
19	use crate::registry::AuthProbe;
20	
21	const DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: u64 = 10;
22	const PROBE_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
23	
24	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
25	pub enum CliAuthStatus {
26	    LoggedIn,
27	    NotLoggedIn { detail: String },
28	    Unknown { reason: String },
29	}
30	
31	/// Run the descriptor's auth probe against `binary` and classify the output.
32	/// Never errors: every failure mode collapses into `Unknown` so the caller
33	/// can fall back to presence-only behavior. `DEADRECKON_AUTH_PROBE=0` (or
34	/// `off`) disables probing entirely — for hermetic test environments that
35	/// redirect `HOME`, where the real CLI would truthfully report logged-out.
36	pub fn probe_cli_auth(binary: &str, probe: &AuthProbe) -> CliAuthStatus {
37	    if matches!(
38	        std::env::var("DEADRECKON_AUTH_PROBE").as_deref(),
39	        Ok("0") | Ok("off") | Ok("false")
40	    ) {
41	        return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
42	            reason: "auth probe disabled by DEADRECKON_AUTH_PROBE".to_string(),
43	        };
44	    }
45	    let timeout = Duration::from_secs(
46	        probe
47	            .timeout_seconds
48	            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS),
49	    );
50	    let mut command = Command::new(binary);
51	    command
52	        .args(&probe.args)
53	        .stdin(Stdio::null())
54	        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
55	        .stderr(Stdio::piped());
56	    let mut child = match command.spawn() {
57	        Ok(child) => child,
58	        Err(err) => {
59	            return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
60	                reason: format!("could not run {binary}: {err}"),
61	            };
62	        }
63	    };
64	    let started = Instant::now();
65	    loop {
66	        match child.try_wait() {
67	            Ok(Some(_)) => break,
68	            Ok(None) => {
69	                if started.elapsed() > timeout {
70	                    let _ = child.kill();
71	                    let _ = child.wait();
72	                    return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
73	                        reason: format!("auth probe timed out after {}s", timeout.as_secs()),
74	                    };
75	                }
76	                std::thread::sleep(PROBE_POLL_INTERVAL);
77	            }
78	            Err(err) => {
79	                return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
80	                    reason: format!("auth probe failed: {err}"),
81	                };
82	            }
83	        }
84	    }
85	    let output = match child.wait_with_output() {
86	        Ok(output) => output,
87	        Err(err) => {
88	            return CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
89	                reason: format!("auth probe failed: {err}"),
90	            };
91	        }
92	    };
93	    let combined = format!(
94	        "{}{}",
95	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
96	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
97	    );
98	    classify_probe_output(probe, &combined)
99	}
100	
101	fn classify_probe_output(probe: &AuthProbe, combined: &str) -> CliAuthStatus {
102	    let condensed = condense(combined);
103	    // Logged-out first: logged-out markers often embed the logged-in phrase
104	    // ("Not logged in" contains "logged in").
105	    if let Some(out_marker) = probe.logged_out_substring.as_deref()
106	        && condensed.contains(&condense(out_marker))
107	    {
108	        return CliAuthStatus::NotLoggedIn {
109	            detail: first_line(combined),
110	        };
111	    }
112	    if let Some(in_marker) = probe.logged_in_substring.as_deref()
113	        && condensed.contains(&condense(in_marker))
114	    {
115	        return CliAuthStatus::LoggedIn;
116	    }
117	    CliAuthStatus::Unknown {
118	        reason: "auth probe output did not match a known login state".to_string(),
119	    }
120	}
121	
122	/// Strip all whitespace so marker matching survives JSON pretty-printing and
123	/// line-wrapping differences between CLI versions.
124	fn condense(text: &str) -> String {
125	    text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect()
126	}
127	
128	fn first_line(text: &str) -> String {
129	    text.lines()
130	        .map(str::trim)
131	        .find(|line| !line.is_empty())
132	        .unwrap_or("no output")
133	        .to_string()
134	}

890	fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
891	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
892	    let mut chars = text.chars();
893	    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
894	        if c == '\u{1b}' {
895	            if chars.next() == Some('[') {
896	                for next in chars.by_ref() {
897	                    if ('@'..='~').contains(&next) {

899	                    }
900	                }
901	            }
902	            continue;
903	        }

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-10 03:18:27Z)**_

Based on my analysis of the changed files:

**Summary of the change**: replaces a custom crossterm raw-mode menu with the `inquire` library across all interactive prompts (`prompt::open`, `select_one`, `confirm`, `ask_number`), and adds a richer `prompt_provider` that surfaces installed subscription CLIs with their login state probed via the pre-existing `probe_cli_auth`.

**Source→sink analysis**:
- `prompt::open`, `select_one`, `confirm`, `ask_number`: pure UI surface. Returns are strings/booleans/usize the caller already had control over; no new authorization, no new persistence.
- `prompt_provider` calls `probe_cli_auth(binary, probe)`, which does `Command::new(binary).args(probe.args)`. Both come from `ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())` — built-in descriptors plus TOML in the user's own `$HOME/providers.d`. Locally trusted; not attacker-influenced. The function ignores stdin and uses `Stdio::null/piped`, so a hostile probe binary can't drive the prompt either. This call path itself is unchanged.
- The "other" branch's free text goes into a provider id used downstream as a registry lookup key; no shell, fs, or HTTP sink is introduced by the diff.
- `prompt_non_git_mode`: the match falls through to `NonGitChoice::Cancel` on any unknown id — fail-closed default. Esc maps to the "cancel" choice via `cancel_choice_index`. No regression of the worktree/copy gate.
- `render_config` only sets terminal colors; no escape-injection sink that the user wouldn't already control.
- Test changes: adds `strip_ansi` (a parser, but only consumes process output for assertions) and sets `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE=1` to keep the PTY test deterministic. No production impact.

No new entry points, no new sinks, no removed validators. The previously-existing `RawModeGuard` is gone, but `inquire` manages its own terminal mode — not a security regression.

No security findings. The diff is essentially a UI refactor (custom raw-mode menu → `inquire`) plus an enriched provider menu that calls a pre-existing auth probe against locally-trusted registry binaries. No new attacker-influenceable source reaches a new sink, and the new fallback paths (`prompt_non_git_mode`'s wildcard match, the "other" provider's empty-input branch) all default to safe behavior.
